brief: Goldman estimates the global oil deficit narrowed from roughly 7mb/d in March to about 1mb/d in Q3 as Gulf supply recovered and demand weakened, so Brent's geopolitical premium can fall without the conflict ending, only needing disruption to stop worsening; CTAs are long oil despite large downside asymmetry if trend levels break. Separately, Goldman models systematic trend followers short about $171mn of global bond DV01, the largest since April 2026, concentrated in Japanese and European rates but also across the US curve. No rate cuts are required to trigger a squeeze: oil stabilizing or softer inflation data could make yields stop rising, forcing short covering into a bond rally, provided intermediate Treasury yields fall while central banks stay hawkish. SOX broke its short-term downtrend toward 12,800, and Goldman's 1-month 110% SOX calls flagged 10 sessions ago have repriced fast, so the desk recommends rolling to higher strikes. JPM's KSTR-versus-KWEB pair, which worked well around May's Trump-Xi summit, should keep working since limited AI cooperation would not remove export controls or China's chip self-sufficiency drive. JPM also argues Brazil at 8.6x forward earnings has priced a new election outcome but not a new economic regime, implying 28-54% upside if valuations rerate.
